findings.title: Specifier.filter() can bypass an explicit prerelease ban
findings.reason: The report identifies missing regression protection for an explicit object-level False, distinct from automatic fallback and method-level overrides. Static tracing supports the suspected implementation bug for the reported setup.
evidence: src/packaging/specifiers.py:245 + Construction stores the explicit setting; line 274 stores an assigned setting.
src/packaging/specifiers.py:598 + Omitting the filter argument forces True into contains(), bypassing the object's False.
src/packaging/specifiers.py:609 + The matching prerelease is buffered; lines 622–624 yield it when nothing else matched.
tests/test_specifiers.py:559 + Existing direct-filter cases cover automatic fallback and a method-level False; lines 565–569 always construct a default Specifier.
tests/test_specifiers.py:730 + Object-level filter overrides construct SpecifierSet; src/packaging/specifiers.py:995 forwards an explicit boolean, avoiding the reported path.
findings.counterevidence: Default fallback is documented at src/packaging/specifiers.py:579 and protected at tests/test_specifiers.py:559. Attribute assignment is also exercised for membership at tests/test_specifiers.py:549. These cover neighboring contracts, not filtering after an explicit object-level ban.

findings.title: Prerelease autodetection can crash a valid arbitrary-equality query
findings.reason: The report identifies an uncovered default-membership path involving an accepted arbitrary target and a valid candidate. Static tracing supports the exception before string comparison. This is a suspected implementation bug plus missing regression protection, within the scoped autodetection behavior.
evidence: src/packaging/specifiers.py:115 + Arbitrary equality promises exact string matching without requiring PEP 440 semantics for the target.
src/packaging/specifiers.py:259 + Autodetection includes ===; line 267 nevertheless parses its target with Version.
src/packaging/version.py:121 + Version requires a numeric release segment; lines 200–202 raise InvalidVersion when parsing fails.
src/packaging/specifiers.py:547 + Direct contains() consults autodetection before reaching the string comparison at line 498.
src/packaging/requirements.py:43 + Requirement exposes a SpecifierSet; src/packaging/specifiers.py:923 consults its prereleases property, which evaluates underlying properties at line 750.
tests/test_specifiers.py:496 + Identity membership cases use valid targets only; lines 588 and 607 inspect operator/version properties for arbitrary targets without membership.
tests/test_requirements.py:86 + Arbitrary targets enter shared parsing cases, whose assertion at line 144 checks specifier equality rather than membership.
src/packaging/utils.py:88 + Canonicalization catches InvalidVersion, explaining why construction and equality assertions do not protect the crashing autodetection path.
findings.counterevidence: Invalid candidate strings are rejected by coercion at src/packaging/specifiers.py:552, but the report deliberately uses valid candidate "1.0". Explicit prerelease arguments bypass autodetection at line 547; marker evaluation supplies True at src/packaging/markers.py:183. Neither disproves the reported default-query gap.

The single historical miss concerns default inclusion below an explicit prerelease bound. src/packaging/specifiers.py:230 promises autodetection, line 259 omits <, and lines 547–558 reject prerelease candidates before the comparator. The comparator at lines 454–465 permits them when the bound itself is a prerelease. tests/test_specifiers.py:522 instead expects False for a prerelease < bound, while the shared comparison assertions force prereleases=True at line 474. Neither report finding identifies this boundary-policy gap. No additional historical misses were counted.

The historical contract has counterevidence in the inclusive-operator comment at src/packaging/specifiers.py:255 and existing False expectations at tests/test_specifiers.py:522–523. The miss assessment concerns the discrepancy between autodetection and the prerelease-bound comparison contract; it does not treat those expectations as protection of the intended policy.
